title.en: 9.6 One view on the future of Indigenous languages
title.zh: 9.6 关于原住民语言未来的一种观点

summary.en: Dr. Kanatawakhon-Maracle argues that Canada should present itself as multilingual rather than bilingual, with Indigenous languages at the table because their speakers were here when English and French arrived. He describes how respect for those languages faded once settlers no longer needed them, and how learning Mohawk means learning Mohawk culture and identity.
summary.zh: Kanatawakhon-Maracle 博士主张，加拿大应把自己说成多语言国家而非双语国家，原住民语言必须坐到谈判桌前，因为英语和法语到来时，这些语言的使用者早已在此。他讲述了一旦定居者不再需要原住民语言，对其的尊重便消失殆尽，并指出学习莫霍克语就是学习莫霍克文化与身份。

points.en: Canada calls itself bilingual, but including the two founding languages plus Indigenous languages still means about fifty-five languages.
points.zh: 加拿大自称双语国家，但把两种建国语言与原住民语言都算进来，仍有大约五十五种语言。

points.en: Early English and French arrivals did learn Indigenous languages out of necessity, because they needed what Indigenous peoples had.
points.zh: 早期的英法到来者出于需要确实学过原住民语言，因为他们需要原住民所拥有的东西。

points.en: Once settlers wanted the land and pushed Indigenous peoples aside, respect for the languages went out the door.
points.zh: 一旦定居者觊觎土地并把原住民赶开，对语言的尊重也就随之荡然无存。

points.en: Language gives Native people a greater sense of who they are, and learning Mohawk means learning Mohawk culture.
points.zh: 语言让原住民更清楚自己是谁，而学习莫霍克语的同时也在学习莫霍克文化。

points.en: He asks to be known by national names such as Mohawk, Oneida, Ojibwe and Chippewa rather than shifting umbrella labels.
points.zh: 他要求人们用莫霍克、奥奈达、奥吉布瓦、齐佩瓦这样的民族名称来认识他们，而不是不断更换的统称标签。

terms.defEn: Languages spoken by the original peoples of a land, before settler colonization.
terms.defZh: 在定居者殖民之前，由某片土地上原有民族使用的语言。

terms.defEn: A nation whose population regularly uses more than two languages.
terms.defZh: 指全国人口日常使用两种以上语言、多语并存的国家情形。

terms.defEn: Settlement and control of a territory and its people by an outside power.
terms.defZh: 外来强权对某片土地及其人民实行定居占领与控制的制度。

terms.defEn: The link between speaking a language and knowing who one is.
terms.defZh: 使用某种语言与确认自身族群身份、文化归属之间的紧密联系。

examples.text: when I was born I was born an Indian but then I became a Native and then I became Aboriginal and then I became First Nations and now I’m Indigenous, yay!
examples.noteEn: He lists the succession of official labels applied to him across his lifetime.
examples.noteZh: 他列举了自己一生中被依次套上的官方标签，用反讽语气呈现这种更名。

examples.noteEn: The national names he would rather be known by than umbrella terms.
examples.noteZh: 他希望人们用来称呼他们的民族名称，而非笼统的统称。

examples.text: If I focus on speaking Mohawk then in the process of learning my language I’m also learning Mohawk culture
examples.noteEn: Learning the language is inseparable from learning the culture that goes with it.
examples.noteZh: 学习语言与学习文化不可分割，二者在同一过程中完成。

body.en: Dr. Kanatawakhon-Maracle argues that Canada, which presents itself as a bilingual country, would do better to describe itself as multilingual. Even if multilingualism were defined as the two founding languages plus the Indigenous languages, he points out, that still amounts to roughly fifty-five languages, and Indigenous languages have to be at the table because their speakers were already here when English and French showed up and built the present-day institutions. Everyone else who comes has, in effect, read the brochure and knows which languages to learn.
body.zh: Kanatawakhon-Maracle 博士认为，自称双语国家的加拿大不如把自己说成多语言国家。他指出，即便把多语言状态界定为两种建国语言加上原住民语言，那也仍然有大约五十五种语言；而且原住民语言必须坐到桌前，因为英语和法语出现并建立当今各种制度时，这些语言的使用者早已在此。其他后来者实际上都读过那份介绍材料，知道自己该学哪种语言。

body.en: He notes that the newcomers did initially learn Indigenous languages in order to deal with their speakers, since they had little choice: Indigenous peoples held what the settlers wanted. When that stopped being true and the land itself became the object, Indigenous peoples were pushed aside and respect for the languages disappeared, after which the assumption became that everyone here speaks English only.
body.zh: 他指出，新来者最初确实学过原住民语言以便与使用者打交道，因为他们别无选择：原住民掌握着定居者想要的东西。而当这一点不再成立、土地本身成为目标时，原住民被推开，对语言的尊重也随之消失，此后便形成了这里人人都只说英语的预设。

body.en: For him the language is a source of identity. Years under the colonial thumb convinced many Native people that their languages and traditions were inferior, but no amount of effort makes a Native person into a non-Native Canadian; focusing on Mohawk means learning Mohawk culture and what it is to be Mohawk. He also resists the sequence of labels — Indian, Native, Aboriginal, First Nations, Indigenous — and asks instead to be known by distinct nationalities and cultures: Mohawk, Oneida, Ojibwe, Chippewa.
body.zh: 对他而言，语言是身份的来源。多年处于殖民统治之下，让许多原住民相信自己的语言和传统低人一等，但无论怎样努力，原住民也不会因此变成非原住民的加拿大人；专注于莫霍克语，就是在学习莫霍克文化以及身为莫霍克人的意义。他也不认同那一连串标签——Indian、Native、Aboriginal、First Nations、Indigenous——而希望人们通过彼此不同的民族与文化来认识他们：莫霍克、奥奈达、奥吉布瓦、齐佩瓦。

summary.en: Chantale Cenerini, a citizen of the Métis Nation Saskatchewan, discusses the multilingual history of the Michif/Métis people, whose large homeland means no single language is shared across the nation. She describes documenting community stories, supporting adult classes and developing an interactive verb game, and the challenges adults face because Michif verbs come from Cree with a complex Algonquian structure.
summary.zh: 梅蒂斯民族萨斯喀彻温公民 Chantale Cenerini 讲述了米奇夫／梅蒂斯人多语言的历史：其家园幅员辽阔，整个民族并不共用一种语言。她介绍了记录社区故事、支持成人课堂和开发互动动词游戏的工作，以及成人学习者因米奇夫语动词源自克里语、具有复杂的阿尔冈昆结构而面临的困难。

points.en: As a post-contact Indigenous people, the Michif/Métis have always been multilingual, dealing with European traders and with Cree, Ojibwe and Saulteaux relatives.
points.zh: 梅蒂斯人与米奇夫人是接触后形成的原住民族群，历来多语并用，与欧洲商人及克里、奥吉布瓦等亲戚往来。

points.en: The Michif homeland spreads across the western provinces and into North Dakota, so communities do not all share one language.
points.zh: 米奇夫家园横跨西部各省并延伸至北达科他，因此各社区并不共用同一种语言。

points.en: Cenerini documents stories told in the community language, which banks the language, gives it prestige and can preserve family history.
points.zh: Cenerini 记录以社区语言讲述的故事，这既保存语言、提升其声望，也可能留存家族历史。

points.en: Community classes pair Elders who speak the language with teachers, linguists and resource developers who support them.
points.zh: 社区课堂把会说语言的老人与教师、语言学家和资源开发者配对，共同提供支持。

points.en: Adult learners struggle because Michif verbs come from Cree and the language has a complex gender system absent from English.
points.zh: 成人学习者困难重重，因为米奇夫语动词来自克里语，且有英语所无的复杂性系统。

points.en: Communities respond better to linguists who genuinely try to learn and speak the language, becoming learners themselves.
points.zh: 社区更认可那些真心努力学习和使用该语言、自己成为学习者的语言学家。

terms.defEn: Efforts by a community to bring back and take ownership of its language.
terms.defZh: 社区为让本族语言回归、由本族掌握并继续使用而开展的努力。

terms.defEn: Recording and archiving a language through stories, texts and audio.
terms.defZh: 通过故事、文本、录音等方式记录并归档一种语言的系统工作。

terms.defEn: A language combining major components, here French nouns and Cree verbs.
terms.defZh: 由不同来源的主要成分组合而成的语言，此处为法语名词加克里语动词。

terms.defEn: A complex verb system typical of Algonquian languages such as Cree.
terms.defZh: 克里语等阿尔冈昆语系语言典型的高度复杂的动词系统。

terms.defEn: Someone learning a family or ancestral language no longer spoken at home.
terms.defZh: 学习家族或祖先语言、但该语言已不在家庭中日常使用的人。

examples.text: Come in with a good heart.
examples.noteEn: Advice from John Medicine Horse Kelly at an ethics institute that stayed with Cenerini.
examples.noteZh: 研究伦理讲习班上一位长者的忠告，Cenerini 始终铭记在心。

examples.text: Round Prairie or La Prairie Ronde
examples.noteEn: A wintering camp whose Michif descendants now live in Saskatoon.
examples.noteZh: 一个冬季营地，其后代米奇夫家庭如今生活在萨斯卡通。

examples.noteEn: The key structural fact that makes Michif verbs unfamiliar to English speakers.
examples.noteZh: 这一关键结构事实使米奇夫语动词对英语母语者十分陌生。

body.en: Chantale Cenerini is an assistant professor at the University of Saskatchewan and a citizen of the Métis Nation Saskatchewan, researching the languages of the Michif/Métis people, Algonquian languages, and French in Manitoba and Saskatchewan. As a post-contact Indigenous people, the Métis and Michifs have always been multilingual, she says, dealing with European traders and settlers as well as with Cree, Ojibwe and Saulteaux relatives. Their homeland spreads across the western provinces and into North Dakota, so no single language is shared by the whole nation; a common consciousness holds it together, and work must be focused locally, community by community.
body.zh: Chantale Cenerini 是萨斯喀彻温大学助理教授，也是梅蒂斯民族萨斯喀彻温的公民，研究米奇夫／梅蒂斯人的语言、阿尔冈昆语系语言以及马尼托巴和萨斯喀彻温的法语。她指出，作为接触后形成的原住民族群，梅蒂斯人和米奇夫人一直多语并用，既与欧洲商人和定居者往来，也与克里、奥吉布瓦、索托的亲戚交流。他们的家园横跨西部各省并延伸至北达科他，整个民族并不共用一种语言，维系他们的是共同的民族意识，因此相关工作必须就地开展，逐社区推进。

body.en: Her role varies from community to community. She documents stories told in the community language — accounts of growing up, family and community history — which bank and document the language while raising its prestige. She also facilitates community-driven projects, including adult classes in Saskatoon taught by speakers who are mostly Elders, with teachers and linguists sharing their skills. From this came resource development, notably an interactive verb game where learners manipulate pieces of a verb to build a sentence, making the Algonquian verb less intimidating. Adults who know only English face a complex gender system and an unfamiliar verb structure, since the verbs come from Cree.
body.zh: 她的角色因社区而异。她记录以社区语言讲述的故事——关于在社区中长大、关于家庭与社区历史的叙述，这些工作既保存和记录语言，也提升其声望。她也为社区主导的项目担任推动者，其中包括萨斯卡通的成人课程：授课者多为老人，教师和语言学家各展所长。由此又发展出资源建设，例如一款互动动词游戏，学习者操作动词的各个成分来造句，让阿尔冈昆语动词不再那么可怕。只会英语的成人要面对复杂的性系统和陌生的动词结构，因为动词来自克里语。

body.en: Michif speakers are at least in their seventies and in demand, so willing teachers are increasingly hard to find; Zoom now lets Saskatoon courses reach Métis people in British Columbia and Regina and reconnect relatives. Communities have had mixed relations with academic linguists, though Peter Bakker’s work is still well regarded, and people think better of researchers who genuinely try to learn and speak the language. The advice Cenerini carried away from an ethics institute led by John Medicine Horse Kelly was simple: come in with a good heart.
body.zh: 米奇夫语的使用者至少已年过七旬且供不应求，愿意授课的人越来越难找；Zoom 让萨斯卡通的课程覆盖到不列颠哥伦比亚和里贾纳的梅蒂斯人，并让亲戚重新联系上。社区与学院派语言学家的关系时好时坏，Peter Bakker 的工作至今仍受敬重，而人们往往更看重那些真心努力学习和使用该语言的研究者。Cenerini 从 John Medicine Horse Kelly 主持的伦理讲习班上带走的一句话很简单：带着善心而来。

summary.en: Rae Anne Claxton, from Tsawout and Cowichan, describes reclaiming Hul’q’umi’num’ within her family after the loss of her grandmother. She discusses the emotional difficulty of adult language learning, the fear of speaking rooted in generations of language loss, and her hope that documentation made by earlier linguists will be returned to communities in accessible forms.
summary.zh: 来自 Tsawout 与 Cowichan 的 Rae Anne Claxton 讲述了在祖母去世后于家族内部重拾 Hul’q’umi’num’ 语的经历。她谈到成人语言学习在情感上的艰难、源于数代语言流失的开口恐惧，以及她的期望：早期语言学家所做的记录能以可用的形式回到社区。

points.en: Claxton heard Hul’q’umi’num’ from her grandparents, who were L1 speakers, but was never encouraged to speak back.
points.zh: Claxton 的祖父母说 Hul’q’umi’num’ 语，是第一语言使用者，但没鼓励她回应。

points.en: After her grandmother, the last fluent speaker in her direct family, died, she began reclaiming the language within her family.
points.zh: 在直系家庭中最后一位流利使用者祖母去世后，她开始在家族内部重拾这门语言。

points.en: Adult learning is emotional and demanding, requiring courage and self-discipline while speakers are being lost and elders are grieved.
points.zh: 成人学习情感负担重且要求高，在使用者不断离世、又要哀悼老人的同时，需要勇气与自律。

points.en: Studying linguistics gave her explanations for phenomena such as the diminutive form her grandmother used for her youngest daughter.
points.zh: 学习语言学让她能解释祖母对年幼女儿使用指小形式这类现象。

points.en: Relations with linguistics have not always been easy, and communities need earlier documentation made accessible to them.
points.zh: 与语言学的关系并不总是顺畅，社区需要能够获取早期所做的语言记录。

points.en: She wants students to know that Indigenous peoples valued linguistic diversity, never forcing others to conform to another language.
points.zh: 她希望学生知道，原住民珍视语言多样性，从不强迫他人改用别的语言。

terms.defEn: The Island dialect of Halkomelem spoken on Vancouver Island.
terms.defZh: 温哥华岛一带使用的哈尔科梅莱姆语岛屿方言，属当地原住民语言。

terms.defEn: The language whose dialects include Island Halkomelem and two Lower Mainland varieties.
terms.defZh: 一个语言，其方言包括岛屿哈尔科梅莱姆语以及低陆平原的两种变体。

terms.defEn: A person who acquired the language as their first language in childhood.
terms.defZh: 在童年时期将该语言作为第一语言自然习得、并以此为主要语言的人。

terms.defEn: A word form marking smallness or endearment, as with a younger child.
terms.defZh: 表示细小、亲昵或年幼的构词形式，如称呼小孩时使用。

terms.defEn: A program pairing a fluent speaker with an adult learner over time.
terms.defZh: 把流利使用者与成人学习者长期配对、共同学习语言的项目。

terms.defEn: An immersion setting where young children are surrounded by the language.
terms.defZh: 让幼儿沉浸在目标语言中的沉浸式照护与语言学习环境。

examples.noteEn: The form her grandmother used for her eldest daughter, later understood as diminutive.
examples.noteZh: 祖母用来称呼她大女儿的形式，她后来才明白这是指小形式。

examples.noteEn: Claxton opens her self-introduction with a Hul’q’umi’num’ greeting of thanks.
examples.noteZh: Claxton 用 Hul’q’umi’num’ 语的致谢问候开始自我介绍。

examples.text: when we lose an elder, we lose a library
examples.noteEn: A saying she cites about the knowledge lost when an Elder dies.
examples.noteZh: 她引用的一句俗语，说明老人去世时随之失去的知识。

examples.text: you can’t do anything without making mistakes. Making mistakes is how you learn
examples.noteEn: Her granny’s reassurance, which she applies to her own speaking.
examples.noteZh: 祖母给她的宽慰，她用来鼓励自己开口说话。

body.en: Rae Anne Claxton was born in Quw’utsun (Cowichan) on Vancouver Island and raised between there and SȾÁUTW̱ (Tsawout First Nation). Her Tsawout grandmother spoke Hul’q’umi’num’, both grandparents in Quw’utsun were L1 speakers, and she learned a little SENĆOŦEN in Saanich. She heard the language and was spoken to in it, but was never encouraged to answer. Hul’q’umi’num’ is the island dialect of Halkomelem, with two further dialects in the Lower Mainland.
body.zh: Rae Anne Claxton 出生于温哥华岛的 Quw’utsun（科维昌），在 Quw’utsun 与 SȾÁUTW̱（Tsawout 第一民族）两地长大。她住在 Tsawout 的祖母说 Hul’q’umi’num’ 语，Quw’utsun 的祖父母都是该语言的第一语言使用者，她在萨尼奇期间还学了一点 SENĆOŦEN 语。她听过这门语言，也被用这门语言搭话，却从未被鼓励开口回应。Hul’q’umi’num’ 语是哈尔科梅莱姆语的岛屿方言，低陆平原还通行另外两种方言。

body.en: After her grandmother, the last fluent speaker in her direct family, died, Claxton began reclaiming the language within her family. She earned a certificate in Hul’q’umi’num’ proficiency at Simon Fraser University, helped establish a Language Nest in Cowichan, worked with children in care through Cowichan Tribes, and developed books, songs and poems for learners. She is in the third year of the First Peoples Cultural Council’s Mentor-Apprentice Program with her si’lu, grandmother Sarah Modeste.
body.zh: 在直系家庭中最后一位流利使用者祖母去世后，Claxton 开始在家族内部重拾这门语言。她在西蒙弗雷泽大学取得 Hul’q’umi’num’ 语语言能力证书，参与在科维昌创建语言巢，通过科维昌部落与寄养儿童一起工作，并为学习者编写书籍、歌曲和诗歌。她目前正与自己的 si’lu（祖母）Sarah Modeste 一起，进入第一民族文化遗产委员会导师—学徒计划的第三年。

body.en: She calls adult language learning emotional, hard work that takes courage, strength and self-discipline, especially as first-language speakers are lost, elders are grieved, and the pandemic removed spaces for conversation. The fear of speaking, which she links to blood memory and generations of language loss, is what she has had to overcome; her granny told her that mistakes are how you learn. Linguistics helped her explain such phenomena as the diminutive her grandmother used for her youngest daughter.
body.zh: 她把成人语言学习形容为需要勇气、力量和自律的艰难情感劳动，尤其是在第一语言使用者不断流失、老人相继离世，而疫情又夺走了会话空间的时候。她说开口的恐惧与血脉记忆以及数代语言流失有关，这正是她必须克服的；祖母告诉她，犯错正是学习的方式。语言学帮助她解释了祖母曾用来称呼小女儿的指小形式这类现象。

body.en: Relations with the field of linguistics have not always been easy, and there is a lack of trust, partly because documentation was made when practising the language could be illegal. Claxton wants that documentation returned to communities in forms meaningful for revitalization. Her grandmother told her she lives in a different time, with access her ancestors were denied. She wants students to know that Indigenous peoples had a culture of understanding linguistics, that many spoke several languages without forcing others to conform, and that her language is alive.
body.zh: 她所在的社区与语言学领域的关系并不总是顺畅，彼此存在不信任，部分原因是当年的语言记录产生于使用这门语言甚至可能违法的年代。Claxton 希望这些记录回到社区，并以对复兴工作有意义的形式呈现。祖母曾告诉她，她生活在一个不同的时代，拥有祖先被剥夺的获取途径。她希望学生知道：原住民本来就有理解语言学的文化，许多人通晓多种语言却从不强迫他人顺从，而且她的语言是活的。
